t38_T1: And if the grown-up you is there, and it's just how deep you're going that's too much, I'd go shallower. Some people try one technique after another instead, to prove to themselves they can take it. Your little one may have had to just take it back then, though. Now there's a grown-up around who can say, "Okay, that's enough for today," and try something gentler instead of giving up on them.
t38_T2: It's different if you're not sure you could stop in the middle and come back, or if turning inward is what's making it worse. Then I'd come all the way back out to the room first. Once you're steadier, try a much smaller door back in, like a quick hello to your little one with your eyes open, before any imagery. It might feel silly, like waving at somebody through a window. Or skip the inside part for now and do one thing the Protector would do for them, out in your life.
t38_T3: If you ever need a full break from your little one, I'd jot down why, and how far you'd gotten before it got to be too much. A couple of lines on your phone is plenty. After a while away, it gets hard to remember. So once that reason has changed and you want to come back, the note tells you where it was still okay. I'd start there, or somewhere a bit gentler.
t38_T4: Whatever you end up trying, I wouldn't go just by how nice a session felt to tell whether it was too much. Grief can come up, or stuff you'd rather never have met, and that by itself doesn't mean anything went wrong. And sometimes you stay right there in the room the whole time and only find out later that it was a lot. Kind of like the gym, where sore and hurt can feel the same at first.
t38_T5: What I'd look at is the next few days. Are you sleeping okay, and getting through your day? Do you kind of want to go back toward whatever came up, or does even thinking about it make you want to hide under the covers? Somewhere in there it usually gets clearer whether it was hard but doable, or just too much.
t38_T6: If you honestly can't tell yet, I wouldn't rush to decide it was a breakthrough, or that it wrecked you. That's a lot to hang on one session. Just make the next one a little easier, and change one thing at a time so it's clear what made the difference. A shorter session, maybe, or a time when you're not already worn out. If you're getting worse from one session to the next, though, change several things at once and get some support. Then work back up to the harder stuff slowly, once you want to and you're bouncing back okay.
t38_T7: Some of what comes up might be a dream that night, or a picture in the middle of a session. So what's it telling you? Probably something about what feels important to you right now, or what you've been needing. It isn't evidence of what happened, though, even when part of you goes, "But I saw it!" I wouldn't build a memory out of it, or let anyone else build one for you.
t38_T8: If being alone was a big part of what hurt in the first place, then reaching toward people is part of taking care of your little one too. Do you have to get yourself sorted out first, so you'll be better company? I really don't think so. If the hurt was being alone, waiting just means more of being alone. So I'd call somebody or show up somewhere, mess and all.
t38_T9: I can't tell you where to look for people who fit you, but I'd bet on more than one place. Keep the good people you've already got. Then maybe try a class, or a spiritual community if one really fits you. Not every one of them has to click (nobody's taking attendance). And if any group, or any one person, starts acting like they should be your only one, that's where I'd want the Protector paying attention.
